evidence: Plaut. Rud. 2.6.47: ut fortūnātī sunt fabrī ferrāriī (Lewis & Short s.v. faber)

terms.comment: A smith in classical Latin is faber with the metal: faber ferrārius, faber aerārius. Every word is classical; we have found no classical instance of the phrase.

sources: Lewis & Short: faber
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 168.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
